4a.note: Official find_miss mixes 0-based and 1-based indexing: it tests A[0]<>B[0] (0-based) but returns B[n+1] when the range empties. 0-based B has indices 0..n, so the missing-at-end case must return B[n]. I ran the official pseudocode literally on 4000 random sorted inputs: 1036 failed, every one the missing-at-end case (B[n+1] out of range); the other 2964 correct. Correct answer: binary search for the first index i with A[i]!=B[i] (monotone since A distinct); return B[i], or B[n] if none. Theta(log n) time, O(1) space. Stored solution reproduces the slip verbatim. Steps (choice, 3, 7, fillblank 'A[middle+1..j],B[middle+1..l]') themselves agree.

5a.note: AVL by barcode + two FIFO queues is correct and meets all bounds (Find/Buy O(log n), Purchase O(1), Supply O(log n)). Slip: in the official Buy, when the month differs it sets amount_month_buy to 0 and does NOT count the current sale, so the first sale of every month is lost and the >49 threshold is off by one for that month; it should set it to 1 (or reset then increment). Also the struct is named tree_Node but typedef'd List_Node (cosmetic) and 'sold at least 50 products' is read per-product (defensible). Steps (queues over stacks, O(log n), 49->queue 2, 50->queue 1) agree.

5b.note: Q1 first, else Q2, dequeue, find in AVL, amount+=50: correct, O(log n). Steps agree (Q1 tested first; third call serves 5).
